**trading** (verb): 1. Carrying on trade or commerce; engaged in trade. 2. Frequented by traders. 3. Venal; corrupt; jobbing.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**cap** (noun): 1. A close-fitting hat, either brimless or peaked. 2. A special hat to indicate rank, occupation, etc. 3. An academic mortarboard.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**progress** (noun): 1. Movement or advancement through a series of events, or points in time; development through time. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. Specifically, advancement to a higher or more developed state; development, growth. 3. An official journey made by a monarch or other high personage; a state journey, a circuit.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**cannot** (verb): 1. Can not; be unable to (whether due to physical inability, logical impossibility, etc.). 2. Be forbidden or not permitted to. 3. Something that cannot be done.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**documentary** (adjective): 1. Of, related to, or based on documents. 2. Which serves to document (record or illustrate) a subject. 3. A film, TV program, publication etc. which presents a social, political, scientific or historical subject in a factual or informative manner.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**delegation** (noun): 1. An act of delegating. 2. The condition of being delegated. 3. A group of delegates.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**director** (noun): 1. One who directs; the person in charge of managing a department or directorate (e.g., director of engineering), project, or production (as in a show or film, e.g., film director). 2. A member of a board of directors. 3. A counselor, confessor, or spiritual guide.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**discriminatory** (adjective): 1. Of or pertaining to discrimination (in all senses). 2. Showing prejudice or bias.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**footballing** (adjective): Relating to the sport of football.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**feature** (noun): 1. One's structure or make-up: form, shape, bodily proportions. 2. An important or main item. A component that draws attention or interest. 3. A component that draws attention or interest.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**gains** (noun): Increase in muscle mass.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**governance** (noun): 1. The process, or the power, of governing; government or administration. 2. The specific system by which a political system is ruled. 3. The group of people who make up an administrative body.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**hub** (noun): 1. The central part, usually cylindrical, of a wheel; the nave. 2. A point where many routes meet and traffic is distributed, dispensed, or diverted. 3. A central facility providing a range of related services, such as a medical hub or an educational hub.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**halt** (verb): 1. To stop marching. 2. To stop either temporarily or permanently. 3. To bring to a stop.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**internal** (adjective): 1. Of or situated on the inside. 2. Within the body. 3. Concerned with the domestic affairs of a nation, state or other political community.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**knockout** (noun): 1. The act of making one unconscious, or at least unable to come back on one's feet within a certain period of time; a TKO. 2. The deactivation of anything. 3. Something wildly popular, entertaining, or funny.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**loan** (noun): 1. An act or instance of lending, an act or instance of granting something for temporary use. 2. A sum of money or other property that a natural or legal person borrows from another with the condition that it be returned or repaid over time or at a later date (sometimes with interest). 3. The contract and array of legal or ethical obligations surrounding a loan.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**mass** (noun): 1. A quantity of matter cohering so as to make one body, or an aggregation of particles or things which collectively make one body or quantity, usually of considerable size. 2. Precious metal, especially gold or silver. 3. A measure of the inertia of a mass of matter, one of four fundamental properties of matter. SI unit of mass: kilogram.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**monarch** (noun): 1. The ruler of an absolute monarchy or the head of state of a constitutional monarchy. 2. A monarch butterfly (Danaus plexippus) and others of genus Danaus, found primarily in North America. 3. A police officer.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**machine** (noun): 1. A vehicle operated mechanically, such as an automobile or an airplane. 2. An answering machine or, by extension, voice mail. 3. A computer.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**often** (adverb): 1. Frequently; many times on different occasions. 2. Frequent.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**perform** (verb): 1. To do (something); to execute. 2. To exhibit an expected pattern of behavior; to function; to work. 3. To act in a way set forth in a contract. To act in accordance with (a contract); to fulfill one’s terms of (a contract).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**receive** (verb): 1. To be given, sent, or paid something. 2. To take, as something that is offered; to accept. 3. To take goods knowing them to be stolen.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**ruled** (adjective): 1. Having printed lines. 2. Being a scroll; being such that through every point of S there is a straight line that lies on S.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**rugby** (noun): 1. Ellipsis of rugby shirt (“a shirt of the kind worn by rugby players, usually short-sleeved and with a buttoned opening at the neck like a polo shirt, but with a stiffer collar”). 2. To play rugby. 3. Rubber cement, contact cement; commonly associated with solvent abuse, as it is often used as an inhalant.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._
